n1.method: Every line and transformer of 100 kV and up is taken out once: with the headline's 14 campuses and their upgrades connected, with all 34 of the search and theirs, and with no campus (the model's own baseline). Flows after each outage come from line outage distribution factors on the network's own factorization (DC power flow; the plants keep their output); a line or transformer is a problem past 115 % of its rating (an assumed emergency rating: the dataset gives one rating). Outages that cut off load are skipped, as the model would strand it on its own. One that cuts off only a plant moves its output to the other plants when they have the room; when they don't, it is a problem of its own (short of generation: the state would have to stop exporting or cut customers). The counts are outages, not overloads: one outage can push several lines past their rating.
n1.sentence: Single-outage screen (N-1) of 2,821 outages, with the headline's 14 campuses and their upgrades: 85 single outages push a line or transformer past 115 % of its rating where the model alone doesn't, or push it further (the model alone has 94 outages that push something past 115 %). With all 34 campuses of the search: 145 single outages push a line or transformer past 115 % of its rating where the model alone doesn't, or push it further; in 194 more, the other plants can't make up the output of a plant the outage cuts off (194 of them would cut customers, up to 1,954 MW).

capacity.method: Campuses go in one at a time, each where it fits with every campus so far (an exact power-flow solve). When none fits, the 30 sites closest to fitting are each solved with the campus there, the lines it would push past their rating are raised to a standard level and priced, and the cheapest bundle is built. With every line in service (N-0), the final set runs through the cascade engine: nothing trips. That checks N-0 only; a single-outage (N-1) screen of the headline's campuses follows. Flexible campuses must fit twice: at full size at 90 % of this load, and at half size at it.

trace.detail: Asked for one more campus for no more than that, or the same 14 for less (the engine's plan needs $69.4M for 15). trace.title: Proposed: 14 campuses with one moved to Haines City

ai.rules: The engine re-solved Gemini's whole plan at once (every campus and every raise): no line or transformer past its rating that wasn't already over with no campus, no load the plants can't supply; each raise sized by the engine's own rule (the flow plus a 10 % margin, in 50 MVA steps, within 5x the original rating) and priced by the engine at the high end (Gemini's own figures are not used); then the full cascade: nothing may trip.
